model: Regulated utility FCFE (attributable net income less equity-funded rate-base growth) at cost of equity (engine route)

inputs.share_count_basis: 328.99M shares outstanding at 30 Sep 2026 (balance sheet / Note 8 roll-forward) plus the Q3-2026 diluted-EPS increment of 2.2M (0.5M stock awards + 1.7M convertible notes; forward-sale contracts by the treasury method are in that figure). Held FLAT: the 7.0M shares sold forward but unsettled (~$764M of proceeds at physical settlement, maturing Sep-2027 to Mar-2028), the rest of the $3.0bn ATM/forward programme and the dividend-reinvestment/benefit-plan issuance are all charged in the flows as equity reinvestment (flow = net income less the FULL increase in common equity, however funded). Growing the count as well would charge them twice.
inputs.sbc_source: Equity-settled stock-based compensation credited to paid-in capital: FY2025 9.0 (WEC_Annual_FY2025.txt:9681), ~2/quarter in 2026 (WEC_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt:5978-5995). Most WEC long-term incentive awards are cash-settled performance units, which are a cash operating cost, not an add-back; the Metrics.csv StockBasedComp figure (48.2 for FY2025) is total expense including those. No equity-award withholding-tax line is disclosed. Net income is already after all of it; the sbc path exists only so the street memo can add the equity-settled part back.
inputs.capital_plan: $47.5bn for 2027-2031 ($42.2bn regulated utilities + $5.3bn share of ATC), up from $37.5bn (FY2025 10-K), $28.0bn and $23.7bn in the two prior plans. Estimated capex 2026 $5.3bn, 2027 $8.4bn, 2028 $9.1bn, of which Wisconsin VLC/Bespoke Resources is $2.1bn / $4.3bn / $5.0bn (WEC_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt:7835, 8913-8919).
inputs.wacc_rationale: The 'wacc' field is a COST OF EQUITY, because the flows are post-interest equity flows. 7.5% = ~4.3% 10-year US Treasury + ~0.6 regulated-utility beta x ~5% US equity risk premium, rounded up; USD flows, USD rate. It is the same rate used for the SO precedent so the two utilities are comparable. The same 7.5% is used in all three scenarios: regulatory, counterparty and execution risk is charged in the scenario ROE/growth paths and the weights, not a second time in the rate.
inputs.net_debt_treatment: net_debt is held at ZERO in the engine. The flow is net income attributed to common shareholders (after ~$0.95bn/yr of interest) less the equity-funded share of rate-base growth, so the $22.76bn of debt (short-term 1,904.3 + current portion 1,134.5 + long-term 19,717.2, including $2.625bn of convertible notes) is already paid for inside the flow. Subtracting it again would deduct the debt twice. total_debt and cash are recorded for reference only.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not modelled separately; lease cost is immaterial (interest on lease liabilities 6.9 in FY2025) and is inside net income.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the flows. Net income is 'attributed to common shareholders' (after the noncontrolling-interest line, +3.6 in 9M-2026, and subsidiary preferred dividends) and the equity base is common shareholders' equity of 14,575.4, which excludes 404.3 of noncontrolling interests (WECI wind/solar partners) and 30.4 of subsidiary preferred stock. Nothing further is deducted in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: equity-flow (FCFE) valuation at the cost of equity, run through the Drivers engine with net debt at zero -- NOT the unlevered owner-FCF DCF. The dcf-methods routing table has no regulated-utility row; this follows the SO (Southern Company) precedent recorded in memory and the skill's principle 'discount the flow the business actually produces, at the rate appropriate to whom it accrues'. Reason: WEC is a rate-regulated utility in a capex supercycle (TTM operating cash flow 3,838 vs capex 4,597; 2027-28 capex of 8.4-9.1bn against ~4-5bn of operating cash flow). Unlevered FCF less $22.7bn net debt gives a meaningless negative number because the capex is not a cost -- it is rate base that earns an allowed return and is ~43-47% equity-financed by regulatory design. The flow that accrues to shareholders is attributable net income minus the increase in common equity needed to hold the capital structure as rate base grows = dividends minus net new share issuance. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue grows at the common-equity (rate-base) growth rate with revenue/common-equity held at the TTM 0.7083x; 'ebitda_margin' = attributable net-income margin + the SBC add-back = ROE / (0.7083 x (1+g)) + 0.09; 'capex' = equity reinvestment = g / (0.7083 x (1+g)); D&A and tax are zero because net income is already after both. So year-t flow = (ROE on opening common equity - g) x opening common equity. Year 1 is the twelve months to 30 Sep 2027. last_fcf is the TTM equity flow on this definition (attributable NI 1,809.5 less the 1,007.0 increase in common equity from 13,568.4 to 14,575.4; cross-check: dividends 1,221 less common stock issued 398 = 823). reported_fcf is TTM OCF 3,837.7 less capex 4,596.8. EARNINGS BASE: TTM reported attributable NI of 1,809.5 includes the $205.0M pre-tax Illinois UEA/QIP rider settlement charge booked in Q4-2025 (~147 after tax) and an 11.9 pre-tax PGL land-sale gain in 2026; adjusted TTM is ~1,948 (~$5.95/share), and 9M-2026 diluted EPS was 4.54 vs 3.85. GUIDANCE ANCHOR (Q3-2026 release/call via the Analysis JSON; not in the 10-K/10-Q): FY2026 EPS $5.60-5.64 (raised from 5.51-5.61); long-term EPS growth 7-8%, upper half from 2028, with commentary pointing to 7-9% under the $47.5bn plan; asset-base CAGR ~13.4% over 2027-31; dividend $3.81. TENSION TO NOTE: 9M-2026 diluted EPS is already 4.54, so the FY2026 range implies only ~$1.08 for Q4-2026 against ~$1.41 adjusted in Q4-2025; either guidance is conservative or 9M carried items that will not repeat (weather, Bespoke carrying-cost timing, tax benefits). The base case leans to guidance rather than extrapolating the 9M beat: year-1 net income ~1,997 (~$6.00/share) vs ~1,948 adjusted TTM. The base equity-growth path of 12-12.5% sits just under the 13.4% asset-base CAGR because the non-VLC utilities are capitalised at ~53% equity and part of the asset growth is debt at the parent. Price is a regular-session close. Buybacks: none (net issuer). SBC is ~0.1% of revenue, so house and street values nearly coincide and the band is degenerate.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3-yr CAGR (6.6%) diverges >30% from revenue (0.7%) and reported EPS (2.6%) 3-yr CAGRs. Revenue is distorted by pass-through gas costs (FY2022 was a gas-price peak) and FY2025 EPS of 4.81 carries a ~0.45/share Illinois settlement charge (ex-charge ~5.27, 3-yr CAGR ~5.8%). Neither is a growth signal.
historical_growth.notes: FY2020-FY2025 and FY2022-FY2025, from Metrics.csv (revenue 7,241.7 / 9,597.4 / 9,800.1; diluted EPS 3.79 / 4.45 / 4.81; total equity 10,662.5 / 11,616.6 / 14,052.8). FCF CAGRs are undefined: reported FCF (OCF less capex) was negative in 5 of the last 7 years and the equity-flow series this model discounts is not a growth series. The historical 5.7% equity CAGR is NOT the forward rate: the capital plan has doubled from $23.7bn to $47.5bn in three years and common equity grew 7.4% in the last twelve months before the 2027-28 capex step-up; the forward path (base 12% stepping down) is built from the plan, not the history.

base.roe_on_opening_common_equity_note: 13.7, 13.6, 13.5, 13.4, 13.2, 13.0, 12.7, 12.4, 12.0, 11.8 percent on opening common equity. Year 1 (~1,997 of net income, ~$6.00/share on ~333M average shares) is set between the guidance-implied figure (~1,977: one quarter of FY2026 at the $5.62 midpoint, three quarters of FY2027 at +7.5%) and the TTM run-rate; years 2-3 give net income growth of ~11-12% and, after ~3%/yr of share issuance, EPS growth of ~8%, inside the 7-9% management range. TTM adjusted ROE on opening common equity was ~14.4% ((1,809.5 reported + ~147 after-tax Illinois rider settlement charge - ~8.5 after-tax PGL land gain) / 13,568.4). Consolidated ROE sits well above the 9.38-9.8% utility allowed ROEs because of holding-company debt (three convertible notes, junior notes and senior notes at the parent), the We Power/WECI non-utility assets and ATC. The path fades 1.9pp as the growth mix shifts to 57%-equity Bespoke Resources at 10.48-10.98% and parent leverage is diluted by ATM equity.
base.terminal_note: Final-year growth equals terminal growth so the terminal flow is a steady-state (ROE - g) x equity. Gordon at 3.0% / 7.5% = 22.9x the net equity flow, about 17x terminal earnings and ~2.0x book, against ~20x adjusted earnings and 2.65x book today.

bull.terminal_note: Gordon binds at 22.9x; ~18x terminal earnings, ~2.2x book.

bear.roe_on_opening_common_equity_note: 13.3, 12.8, 12.3, 11.8, 11.3, 11.0, 10.8, 10.5 thereafter, percent on opening common equity.
bear.terminal_note: The 20x cap binds just below Gordon (20.5x); ~15x terminal earnings, ~1.6x book.

scenario_narratives.base: The $47.5bn 2027-31 plan is executed broadly on schedule. Common equity (a proxy for the equity slice of rate base) grows 12-12.5% a year through 2029, funded by ~0.8bn/yr of retained earnings plus ~1.0-1.2bn/yr of ATM/forward equity, then slows as the Microsoft and Vantage/Oracle build-out completes after 2031. ROE on opening equity fades from 13.7% to 11.8% as the mix shifts to Bespoke Resources (10.48-10.98% ROE, 57% equity, fixed for the contract term) and parent leverage is diluted. Net equity flow is close to zero for three years (dividends roughly offset by issuance) and the value sits in the terminal: ~17x earnings, ~2.0x book.
scenario_narratives.bull: Large-load demand exceeds the 4.5GW in the plan (3.2GW Microsoft corridor + 1.3GW Vantage), the capital plan is raised again as it has been in each of the last three years, the 2027-28 Wisconsin rate orders prove sufficient to earn the allowed ROE, and EPS growth runs at the top of the 7-9% range. Equity compounds 13.5-14% for three years with ROE held at ~14% by Bespoke carrying-cost revenue and AFUDC. More growth at a ~7pp spread over the cost of equity is worth more, but it defers cash: flows are thinner than base until year 6.
scenario_narratives.bear: A VLC downsizes or delays (Microsoft has paused phases before; Oracle's parent has already been downgraded and is posting collateral), so the Bespoke build is stretched and the plan shrinks. The tariff's take-or-pay and collateral terms protect invested capital but not the growth. Separately the PSCW, which already granted less than requested in the 2027-28 Wisconsin cases, keeps trimming on affordability, the negative rating outlook at WPS forces more equity sooner, Illinois stays hostile (9.38% ROE, PRP paused, $130M rate-base write-off), and higher-for-longer rates squeeze the levered parent. Equity growth falls to 9% then 5%, ROE fades to 10.5%, and the exit multiple is capped at 20x the equity flow (~15x earnings).

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20%, above the 15% house default: half of 2027-28 Wisconsin capex is for two or three very large customers, one of whose parents has been downgraded, and Illinois has shown it will disallow. Not the 25% used for SO, because the adverse regulatory event has not happened here -- the PSCW approved the VLC and Bespoke Resources tariffs in May 2026 with cost-shift protections, the contracts require reimbursement and collateral, and Wisconsin has a long constructive record. Bull 30%, below the 35% default: it needs the plan to be raised again AND the ROE to hold through a rate case while the equity is being issued.

valuation_philosophy.summary: WEC is valued as an equity compounder under a regulated return: each dollar of common equity earns ~12-14% and the question is how many dollars the regulators and the large-load customers will let it deploy, and how much of that must be raised from shareholders. Value = present value of (ROE - growth) x equity at a 7.5% cost of equity. Because the supercycle absorbs nearly all earnings plus new equity for several years, 75-85% of value is terminal -- the result is most sensitive to the steady-state ROE and the cost of equity, not to near-term EPS. A 15% hurdle is not reachable in a regulated utility earning ~10% allowed returns; the entry price at the hurdle is reported for consistency across the folder and is not a realistic bid.
key_risks_to_valuation: Customer concentration: Microsoft (up to 3.2GW) and Vantage/Oracle (1.3GW) drive roughly half of 2027-28 Wisconsin capex; OACS's parent has already been downgraded

Wisconsin regulation: the 2027-28 rate orders came in below the request; allowed ROE (~9.8%) and the earnings-sharing mechanism cap the upside while equity issuance peaks; a rating agency has WPS on negative outlook
Illinois: 9.38% ROE, $205M rider settlement charge in 2025, $130M removed from rate base from 2027, pipe-replacement programme under ICC control

Financing: ~$22.8bn debt, $2.6bn of convertibles maturing 2027-29, and an equity need that rises with every plan increase -- issuance below ~2.5x book destroys less value than it seems only while the price holds
Cost of equity: +/-50bp moves the base value by roughly 12-15%
FY2026 guidance ($5.60-5.64) implies a much weaker Q4 than the 9M run-rate; if the 9M beat is structural the base case is ~3% too low, if it was weather it is about right
